PlayStation 2.text: Its last game, Pro Evolution Soccer 2014, came out in Europe in November 2013.
PlayStation 2.evidence: it remained in production and continued to receive new game releases for several years with the last game for the system Pro Evolution Soccer 2014 being released exclusively in Europe on 8 November 2013.

Nintendo Switch.text: Its Joy-Con controllers work as two halves of one controller or as two separate ones.
Nintendo Switch.evidence: Its wireless Joy-Con controllers function as two halves of a standard controller and alternatively as individual controllers,

Nintendo DS.text: The "DS" stands for "Dual Screen"; the lower of its two screens is a touchscreen.
Nintendo DS.evidence: The "DS" in the name is an initialism for "Dual Screen", reflecting the system's most distinctive feature: two LCD screens working in tandem, with the lower screen functioning as a touchscreen.

Game Boy.text: In North America and Europe it came bundled with Tetris.
Game Boy.evidence: In North America and Europe, the Game Boy was backed by a large marketing campaign and bundled with Tetris, which increased its appeal beyond traditional video game audiences.

PlayStation 4.text: According to lead architect Mark Cerny, work on it began as early as 2008.
PlayStation 4.evidence: According to lead architect Mark Cerny, the development of Sony's fourth video game console began as early as 2008.

PlayStation.text: Sony built it after a failed venture with Nintendo on a CD-ROM add-on for the Super Nintendo.
PlayStation.evidence: Sony began developing the PlayStation after a failed venture with Nintendo to create a CD-ROM peripheral for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System in the early 1990s.

Wii.text: During development it was codenamed Revolution.
Wii.evidence: Shigeru Miyamoto and Genyo Takeda led development, which was initially codenamed Revolution.

PlayStation 5.text: A central challenge in its development was cutting game loading times.
PlayStation 5.evidence: During the development of the PlayStation 5, a central challenge revolved around addressing the length of loading times for games.

PlayStation 3.text: The first console to use Blu-ray as its main storage medium, and the first with an HDMI port.
PlayStation 3.evidence: It was the first console to use the Blu-ray disc as its primary storage medium, the first to be equipped with an HDMI port, and the first capable of outputting games in 1080p (Full HD) resolution.

Xbox 360.text: Early units failed so often, with the "Red Ring of Death", that Microsoft had to extend the warranty.
Xbox 360.evidence: The earliest versions of the console suffered from a high failure rate, indicated by the so-called "Red Ring of Death", necessitating an extension of the device's warranty period.
